concepts.title: Śāṇḍilya Says It and the Purāṇas Do Not — the Corpus Naming an Absence and Routing Around It

concepts.title: Datta Is the Doorway, Bhairava Is the Experience — and the Practitioner Is What Has to Be Ready
concepts.excerpt: The episode's last thirty seconds carry its most compact doctrine, and the corpus flags it as personal before delivering it: "Datta, I personally feel this — as well as this is what is being taught in our sampradāya: Datta is a doorway, Bhairava is an experience.

concepts.title: The Roster as This Corpus Tells It — Twenty-Four Teachers, Numbered Aloud, and the Count Does Not Close
concepts.excerpt: The Avadhūta's twenty-four teachers are one of the best-known passages in the Purāṇic literature.

concepts.title: Knowledge, But Not the Knower — the Corpus Adds a Twenty-Fifth Guru to a List That Has Always Ended at Twenty-Four
concepts.excerpt: The Avadhūta finishes reciting his twenty-four teachers, the king is speechless, and then the corpus does something no received telling of this discourse does.

concepts.title: The Voice That Says "I Should Practise" Is the Thing You Were Going to Practise For
concepts.excerpt: The corpus's most useful teaching about awareness is not a definition.

concepts.title: A King Asks a Naked Wanderer Why He Is Happy — and the Answer Takes an Hour
concepts.excerpt: The frame that carries the twenty-four-guru discourse is small and does specific work.

concepts.title: Eighty-Four Classrooms, Not Eighty-Four Sentences — and the Arithmetic Closes
concepts.excerpt: > This concept requires both a doctrine of rebirth and a developmental account of what each embodiment teaches, simultaneously, because the framework's whole claim is that the sequence is pedagogical rather than punitive — and a cosmology of rebirth alone cannot say what is learned, while a developmental psychology alone has no account of why the sequence spans species.

concepts.title: "I Must Live" and Not Yet "Why Am I Living" — the First Circle, and Where Sensitivity Begins
concepts.excerpt: Nine lakh aquatic births, and the corpus reduces the whole class to one sentence a jīva can hold and one it cannot yet.

concepts.title: "As Long as Necessary" — the Tree's Lesson, and Why Stillness Comes Before Meditation
concepts.excerpt: Twenty lakh plant births, and the corpus answers the obvious objection before it is raised.

concepts.title: The Bird Can Cross the Sky and Is Still Hungry — the Distinction That Makes the Whole Map Work
concepts.excerpt: Ten lakh bird births, and the corpus spends most of the circle setting up one sentence.

concepts.title: "Emotion Is Not the Enemy — Emotion Is a Stage of the Consciousness"
concepts.excerpt: Thirty lakh animal births — the largest circle in the scheme by a wide margin — and the corpus refuses the move a renunciate reading would make.

concepts.title: "More Alive" — and the One Question That Constitutes the Human Birth
concepts.excerpt: Four lakh human births — the smallest circle in the scheme — and the corpus refuses to define it by anatomy, capability or dominance.

concepts.title: Six From the Guru, Three From the Teacher — a Ninefold List That Discloses Its Own Seam
concepts.excerpt: The corpus gives nine faculties of the human birth and then does something almost no source in this build does: it tells you which ones are not in the story.

concepts.title: Four Conversions, Not One Renunciation — What the Human Birth Can Do With Thirty Lakh Births' Worth of Feeling
concepts.excerpt: The corpus knows this will be heard as wordplay and says so before making the claim.

concepts.title: The Seventh Circle Is Not a Birth — Twelve Stages Inside the Human One, Ending in Bhairava-Bhāva
concepts.excerpt: Six circles account for eighty-four lakh births and the corpus says they are only the doorway.

concepts.title: "84 Classrooms" — The Closing Move That Turns a Sentence Into a Syllabus
concepts.excerpt: Eighty-eight minutes of counted births end on a sentence that removes the counting.

concepts.title: Tarpaṇa Refused on a Grievance — Settling Accounts With the Dead
concepts.excerpt: The corpus puts the objection in the practitioner's own mouth, in the words it apparently arrives in:

concepts.title: Sarpa-Doṣa Is an Imprint, Not an Event — and the Corpus Reads It on Four Instruments
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ The whole episode turns on one refusal: sarpa-doṣa is not a thing that happened.

concepts.title: One Pūjā Clears One Layer — and Karma Is Not Linear
concepts.excerpt: The question the passage answers is the one every returning client asks.

concepts.title: The Debt Attaches to the Plot, Not to the Person Who Incurred It
concepts.excerpt: The corpus reaches its universality claim by a route nobody expects: property.

concepts.title: Two Tiers of Remedy — the Full Sarpa-Doṣa Protocol, Including the Half That Costs Nothing
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ The corpus splits the treatment in two and says so explicitly. "The true healing of the sarpa-doṣa happens in the two layers: one is actually outer remedies, one is inner remedies."

concepts.title: Memory Without Knowledge, Time Without Urgency, Power Without Expression
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ The corpus's most compressed statement about what a nāga is comes with the psychological reading attached, unprompted.

concepts.title: The Guardian Whose Trigger Condition Is Forgetting
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ Most manifestation narratives in this corpus begin with a demon or a petition.

concepts.title: The Consort the Corpus Says Is in No Book
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ The corpus stops and marks its own provenance before it says the name, which it does almost nowhere else in thirty-four sources.

concepts.title: The Corpus Grades One of Its Own Sources Down — and Says the Practice Survives in Two States
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ Across roughly thirty named texts this corpus assigns a genre to exactly one.

concepts.title: Vāsuki: The One Who Was Used as Equipment and Called It Devotion
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ The corpus's claim about the first of the eight is not that Vāsuki was strong.

concepts.title: Śeṣa-Ananta: The Only One in the Roster Whose Function Is to Not Move
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ Seven of the eight nāgas teach by doing something. "Ananta teaches us: be still.

concepts.title: Takṣaka: The Debt That Waits Two Generations and Then Collects
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ The third of the eight is the only one in the roster who is not a teacher but an enforcement mechanism.

concepts.title: Mahāpadma: The Treasure-Keeper Whose Access Condition Is That You Stop Reaching
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ The fourth of the eight is the roster's wealth-form, and the corpus immediately removes the obvious reading.

concepts.title: Kulika: The Serpent Who Holds the Texts That Were Never Released
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ The fifth of the eight is the one the corpus says is least spoken of, and he is given the roster's most consequential office.

concepts.title: Karkoṭaka: The Poison That Turns Out to Have Been the Help
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ The sixth of the eight is the roster's only one who does damage first and is credited for it afterwards.

concepts.title: Padmanāga: Still the Water and You Can See Through It
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ The seventh of the eight is the only one whose office is a medium rather than a virtue.

concepts.title: Śaṅkhapāla: The Eighth Is a Voice That Only Says *Not This*
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ The roster closes on the quietest of the eight and the corpus gives him the smallest possible signal.

concepts.title: Forty-One Shelf Rows, Three Division-Level References, and One Chapter Number
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ This page is a finding aid, not a verdict. It answers one question a reader of this corpus repeatedly needs answered: when a text is named, what is a reader given, and what can be followed up?

concepts.title: The Purāṇa the Corpus Reaches For When Śiva Is Not the One Who Acts
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ The Devī Purāṇa is the second-most-invoked purāṇa in this corpus and it is invoked for a consistent purpose: every time it is named, the Devī is doing something Śiva is not.

concepts.title: The Dog on the Last Walk Is Not a Companion — It Is Bhairava's Own Awareness
concepts.excerpt: ⚑⚑ The corpus's death material is sourced to four texts and none of them supplies its sharpest claim.
